chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ubayd Allah al-Halabi, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Goods were brought to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from Egypt, so he prepared food and invited the merchants. They said, 'We will take it from you for nine thousand.' He asked them, 'And how much is that?' They said, 'Two thousand for every ten thousand.' He said, 'I will sell you this goods for twelve thousand.'

key_terms.دَهْ دَوَازْدَهْ: Nine thousand (a specific numerical expression used in the narration)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith regarding trade discounts and pricing strategies of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) mastery of market dynamics, where he rejected a fixed percentage discount in favor of a lump-sum valuation, thereby avoiding the ambiguity (*gharar*) often associated with proportional deductions. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on transparency and mutual consent in commercial transactions, ensuring that the final price is clearly defined and agreed upon by both parties. This narrative serves as a practical model for merchants to maximize value while maintaining ethical integrity in trade.
